newsitem.title: BELGIUM: RENAULT TO STOP CAR PRODUCTION IN BELGIUM.
newsitem.headline: RENAULT TO STOP CAR PRODUCTION IN BELGIUM.

text.p: French car maker Renault is to close its Belgian car plant at Vilvoorde, near Brussels, on July 31 with the loss of 3,100 jobs, a spokesman for the Belgian unit confirmed on Thursday.
"This was not expected," spokesman Martin Bart told Reuters.
The plant's production of Renault's Megane and Clio models would be moved elsewhere. The plant had a capacity of 143,000 cars a year, he said.

In a statement, Renault blamed the move on poor results, which in 1996 would be "overwhelmingly negative." It said with the closure of the Belgian plant it would be concentrating its Megane production on two sites, in Douai, France, and Palencia, Spain.
Renault said it would seek to employ 1,900 of the Belgian workers at its other plants.

The closure is likely to send huge shivers through the Belgian economy, which also boasts major Ford , Opel and Volvo car plants. Renault said it would look for another manufacturer to take over its Belgian plant.
Political reaction was slow, perhaps indicative of the fact that no-one was expecting the announcement.
Vilvoorde's residents include Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene, who visited the factory as recently as Saturday to present merit awards to some of its employees.
